← Back to search

Radboud’s English-taught Artificial Intelligence bachelor studies human cognition and develops intelligent computer systems. Programming, mathematics, statistics, robotics, neuroscience, language and philosophy support a 180 EC degree with restricted electives, free choice and a required thesis.

Three related UCR programmes emphasise broad AI and cognition, computational intelligent systems, or cognitive neuroscience and language. Each contains substantial AI methods but differs from Radboud’s integrated specialist sequence. Human language study is distinct from computational NLP, and the UCR schedules do not replace the separate Radboud thesis.

Academic year: 2026–2027

This pathway uses the current 2026–2027 regulations. Prospective webpages describe an indicative overview that may change; future cohort availability is not guaranteed. Year 2 contains 12 EC restricted choices and year 3 contains 24 EC restricted choices plus 24 EC free electives. The cohort 2025-only Cognitive Science option is excluded. Year 2 requires positive study advice; year 3 requires all first-year units; the thesis requires 120 EC. RADAr English is an additional 0 EC requirement. The programme publishes a 42 EC first-year continuation threshold, subject to personal circumstances.

What this comparison shows

A curriculum-level comparison of Artificial Intelligence at Radboud University with 3 illustrative UCR study compositions.

CLOSEST UCR MATCH
Artificial intelligence, cognition & intelligent systems

Programming, mathematical methods and machine learning combine with robotics, reinforcement learning, signal processing and cognitive neuroscience. Human perception, higher cognition and language supply the cognitive-science strand of this broad AI programme.

ADDITIONAL UCR OPTION
Computational AI & autonomous systems

Programming, algorithms, software, data infrastructure and mathematical modelling organise this computational AI programme. Machine learning, reinforcement learning, robotics and computer vision develop intelligent systems, supported by research methods, AI ethics and an introduction to brain and behaviour.

ADDITIONAL UCR OPTION
Cognitive AI, language & neuroscience

Cognitive neuroscience, human language, psychology and philosophy organise this cognitive AI programme. Programming, machine learning, neural networks, computer vision, optimisation and statistics connect the study of mind and brain to computational methods; research training includes experimental design and evidence synthesis.

Important limitation

This is a curriculum comparison. A UCR composition is not the same disciplinary degree and does not by itself establish a professional qualification or automatic eligibility for a particular master’s programme.

Rows show curricular relationships, including partial matches, rather than course equivalence. A blank cell means there is no closely comparable component in that row. Optional independent research is additional to the displayed 180 EC.

modals.text:
Personal & Professional Development
This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.
Close

Research Methods & Statistics
Research Methods & Statistics introduces research design, operationalisation, sampling, experiments and surveys. Students study descriptive and inferential statistics, association, hypothesis testing and analysis of variance, with an introduction to multivariate applications. A group research project applies these methods to a chosen research problem.
Close

AI Ethics
AI Ethics examines artificial intelligence from philosophical and psychological perspectives. Topics include fairness and bias, privacy, responsibility, accountability, the moral status of AI systems and broader political risks. Students also consider trust and decision-making, empathy and confidentiality in clinical settings, algorithmic stereotypes, and how AI companions and tutors may affect children’s learning and relationships.
Close

Decision-making in AI
Introduces planning techniques for AI systems in deterministic and non‑deterministic environments. Addresses uncertainty, partial observability, resource planning and optimizing behaviour under constraints.
Close

Logic & Discrete Mathematics
Focuses on mathematics of decision‑making, covering topics in discrete mathematics such as logic, patterns and structures, with applications to computer science and algorithm construction.
Close

Optimization Methods in AI
Optimization Methods in AI studies search and optimisation for rational agents. Topics include uninformed and informed search, local and global search, adversarial games and constraint satisfaction. Laboratory exercises and projects include graph search, convex optimisation, and linear and nonlinear programming.
Close

Reinforcement Learning
Explores reinforcement learning. Covers theoretical frameworks and algorithms and requires students to implement algorithms and build agents using neural networks that learn through trial and error.
Close

Networks & Operating Systems
Introduces computer networks and operating systems. Covers how the internet works and the role of an OS in resource management and application support.
Close

Database Management Systems
Introduces relational database management systems and SQL. Covers relational database theory, authorization, normalization and query processing.
Close

Software Development
Covers software design, creation, testing and maintenance. Uses C++ and Haskell and covers planning, requirements gathering, testing, deployment and maintenance through discussions and code reviews.
Close

Algorithms & Data Structures
Teaches design and analysis of algorithms and data structures, emphasizing performance analysis and focusing on prominent algorithms and data structures.
Close

Advanced Algorithms
Studies modern algebraic algorithms and optimization methods. Emphasises algorithmic thinking and mathematical modelling of computational problems.
Close

Introduction to Data Science
Develops foundational skills in data visualization, cleaning and manipulation. Explores spatial and text data and includes hands‑on work with datasets from various disciplines.
Close

Machine Learning
Machine Learning introduces methods for understanding data and making predictions, including linear regression, classification, resampling, shrinkage, tree-based methods, support vector machines and clustering. Real-world examples illustrate the methods, their strengths and limitations.
Close

Image Processing & Computer Vision
Image Processing & Computer Vision studies how structural information is extracted from images and video. Topics include camera and colour models, filtering, edge and feature detection, segmentation, tracking and object recognition. Practical work develops computational image-analysis skills, with applications including medical imaging and remote sensing.
Close

Neural Networks & Deep Learning
Neural Networks & Deep Learning combines theory with practical Python implementations. Students build and train networks, use TensorFlow, and study applications to tabular data, computer vision and text classification. Recent language-model developments are discussed; image-generation models may be considered if time permits.
Close

Robotics
Covers computational problems in robotics. Includes forward and inverse kinematics, motion planning, collision avoidance and robotic grasping and manipulation.
Close

Introduction to Programming
Introduces programming and computer science. Covers structured programming, data constructs, testing, debugging and object‑oriented programming with Python, and develops computational problem‑solving skills.
Close

Mathematical Methods
Mathematical Methods develops foundational techniques in differentiation, integration, complex numbers and differential equations. Students solve mathematical problems and apply these techniques in projects drawing on fields such as science, economics and sociology.
Close

Linear Algebra
Linear Algebra studies systems of equations, matrices, vectors, linear transformations and vector spaces. Students examine determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and applications including Fourier series, difference equations and Markov chains.
Close

Computational & Numerical Methods
Introduces numerical methods such as root‑finding, interpolation, numerical differentiation and integration and solving differential equations. Emphasises algorithm accuracy, stability and efficiency and uses computer algebra software.
Close

Linear Systems
Linear Systems studies signals and linear time-invariant systems. Students examine impulse and frequency responses, convolution, Fourier series and transforms, and the Laplace and Z transforms, including continuous-time and discrete-time representations.
Close

Probability & Statistics
Provides a foundation in mathematical statistics. Covers probability theory, discrete and continuous distributions, sampling, parameter estimation and simulation; uses computer algebra software to develop theoretical understanding and practical skills.
Close

Philosophy of Mind
Examines historical and modern work on the philosophy of mind. Discusses Descartes’ dualism, the nature of consciousness, AI and animal minds, personal identity, transformative experiences and the influence of technology on experience.
Close

Free Will, Time & the Self
Investigates concepts of free will, the role of luck and openness of the future. Explores relations between free will, time and the self across multiple modules and contemporary debates.
Close

Neurobiology
Neurobiology studies the biological basis of behaviour through evolutionary pressures, biorhythms, comparative anatomy, animal models and selected disorders. Students examine research ethics and animal welfare, practise laboratory techniques such as microscopy and cell staining, and compare brain anatomy across species.
Close

Perception & Action
Explores neural mechanisms behind perception and action. Examines how the brain processes sensory information and guides goal‑directed behaviour using methods from cognitive neuroscience and neuropsychology.
Close

Higher Order Functions
Higher Order Functions deepens knowledge of neurophysiology, neuroanatomy and experimental cognitive neuroscience. Topics include memory, emotion, social cognition, attention, consciousness, decision-making and planning. Students evaluate current research and develop experimental designs.
Close

Psycholinguistics
Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.
Close

Introduction to Brain & Behavior
Explores why people behave as they do and how brain injuries affect mental processes. Discusses nature and nurture, introduces brain anatomy and psychological theories, and provides a gateway to cognitive science and clinical psychology.
Close

Social Psychology
Covers main theories, findings and principles of social psychology, emphasising its scientific approach to understanding how people’s feelings, thoughts and behaviour are influenced by the presence of others.
Close

Statistics & Experimental Methods
Teaches multivariate statistical methods for research on complex human phenomena. Topics include linear and logistic regression, factor analysis, analysis of variance and covariance, and non-parametric tests. Students select and apply models, assess statistical problems and report their analyses.
Close

Advanced Research Seminar
Advanced Research Seminar introduces systematic reviews and meta-analysis to synthesise results across studies. Students use R to conduct analyses, work with data structures and packages, estimate treatment effects and examine their consistency across studies. Presentations and active research tasks develop evidence-synthesis skills.
Close

Lifespan Developmental Psychology
Explores human development across the lifespan. Examines physical, cognitive, emotional and social changes from prenatal life to old age and develops critical thinking about factors influencing individual uniqueness.
Close

UCR can construct substantial AI programmes with different computational and cognitive emphases. They retain gaps in dedicated Bayesian methods, NLP, human-centred design, brain-computer interfacing and theoretical cognitive modelling. Signal processing is present only in the broad UCR programme. Evidence synthesis and other scheduled research work do not replace Radboud’s separate thesis; optional independent research is additional to the 24-course plan.

modals.text:
Personal & Professional Development
This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.
Close

Research Methods & Statistics
Research Methods & Statistics introduces research design, operationalisation, sampling, experiments and surveys. Students study descriptive and inferential statistics, association, hypothesis testing and analysis of variance, with an introduction to multivariate applications. A group research project applies these methods to a chosen research problem.
Close

AI Ethics
AI Ethics examines artificial intelligence from philosophical and psychological perspectives. Topics include fairness and bias, privacy, responsibility, accountability, the moral status of AI systems and broader political risks. Students also consider trust and decision-making, empathy and confidentiality in clinical settings, algorithmic stereotypes, and how AI companions and tutors may affect children’s learning and relationships.
Close

Decision-making in AI
Introduces planning techniques for AI systems in deterministic and non‑deterministic environments. Addresses uncertainty, partial observability, resource planning and optimizing behaviour under constraints.
Close

Logic & Discrete Mathematics
Focuses on mathematics of decision‑making, covering topics in discrete mathematics such as logic, patterns and structures, with applications to computer science and algorithm construction.
Close

Optimization Methods in AI
Optimization Methods in AI studies search and optimisation for rational agents. Topics include uninformed and informed search, local and global search, adversarial games and constraint satisfaction. Laboratory exercises and projects include graph search, convex optimisation, and linear and nonlinear programming.
Close

Reinforcement Learning
Explores reinforcement learning. Covers theoretical frameworks and algorithms and requires students to implement algorithms and build agents using neural networks that learn through trial and error.
Close

Networks & Operating Systems
Introduces computer networks and operating systems. Covers how the internet works and the role of an OS in resource management and application support.
Close

Database Management Systems
Introduces relational database management systems and SQL. Covers relational database theory, authorization, normalization and query processing.
Close

Software Development
Covers software design, creation, testing and maintenance. Uses C++ and Haskell and covers planning, requirements gathering, testing, deployment and maintenance through discussions and code reviews.
Close

Algorithms & Data Structures
Teaches design and analysis of algorithms and data structures, emphasizing performance analysis and focusing on prominent algorithms and data structures.
Close

Advanced Algorithms
Studies modern algebraic algorithms and optimization methods. Emphasises algorithmic thinking and mathematical modelling of computational problems.
Close

Introduction to Data Science
Develops foundational skills in data visualization, cleaning and manipulation. Explores spatial and text data and includes hands‑on work with datasets from various disciplines.
Close

Machine Learning
Machine Learning introduces methods for understanding data and making predictions, including linear regression, classification, resampling, shrinkage, tree-based methods, support vector machines and clustering. Real-world examples illustrate the methods, their strengths and limitations.
Close

Image Processing & Computer Vision
Image Processing & Computer Vision studies how structural information is extracted from images and video. Topics include camera and colour models, filtering, edge and feature detection, segmentation, tracking and object recognition. Practical work develops computational image-analysis skills, with applications including medical imaging and remote sensing.
Close

Neural Networks & Deep Learning
Neural Networks & Deep Learning combines theory with practical Python implementations. Students build and train networks, use TensorFlow, and study applications to tabular data, computer vision and text classification. Recent language-model developments are discussed; image-generation models may be considered if time permits.
Close

Robotics
Covers computational problems in robotics. Includes forward and inverse kinematics, motion planning, collision avoidance and robotic grasping and manipulation.
Close

Introduction to Programming
Introduces programming and computer science. Covers structured programming, data constructs, testing, debugging and object‑oriented programming with Python, and develops computational problem‑solving skills.
Close

Mathematical Methods
Mathematical Methods develops foundational techniques in differentiation, integration, complex numbers and differential equations. Students solve mathematical problems and apply these techniques in projects drawing on fields such as science, economics and sociology.
Close

Linear Algebra
Linear Algebra studies systems of equations, matrices, vectors, linear transformations and vector spaces. Students examine determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and applications including Fourier series, difference equations and Markov chains.
Close

Computational & Numerical Methods
Introduces numerical methods such as root‑finding, interpolation, numerical differentiation and integration and solving differential equations. Emphasises algorithm accuracy, stability and efficiency and uses computer algebra software.
Close

Linear Systems
Linear Systems studies signals and linear time-invariant systems. Students examine impulse and frequency responses, convolution, Fourier series and transforms, and the Laplace and Z transforms, including continuous-time and discrete-time representations.
Close

Probability & Statistics
Provides a foundation in mathematical statistics. Covers probability theory, discrete and continuous distributions, sampling, parameter estimation and simulation; uses computer algebra software to develop theoretical understanding and practical skills.
Close

Philosophy of Mind
Examines historical and modern work on the philosophy of mind. Discusses Descartes’ dualism, the nature of consciousness, AI and animal minds, personal identity, transformative experiences and the influence of technology on experience.
Close

Free Will, Time & the Self
Investigates concepts of free will, the role of luck and openness of the future. Explores relations between free will, time and the self across multiple modules and contemporary debates.
Close

Neurobiology
Neurobiology studies the biological basis of behaviour through evolutionary pressures, biorhythms, comparative anatomy, animal models and selected disorders. Students examine research ethics and animal welfare, practise laboratory techniques such as microscopy and cell staining, and compare brain anatomy across species.
Close

Perception & Action
Explores neural mechanisms behind perception and action. Examines how the brain processes sensory information and guides goal‑directed behaviour using methods from cognitive neuroscience and neuropsychology.
Close

Higher Order Functions
Higher Order Functions deepens knowledge of neurophysiology, neuroanatomy and experimental cognitive neuroscience. Topics include memory, emotion, social cognition, attention, consciousness, decision-making and planning. Students evaluate current research and develop experimental designs.
Close

Psycholinguistics
Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.
Close

Introduction to Brain & Behavior
Explores why people behave as they do and how brain injuries affect mental processes. Discusses nature and nurture, introduces brain anatomy and psychological theories, and provides a gateway to cognitive science and clinical psychology.
Close

Social Psychology
Covers main theories, findings and principles of social psychology, emphasising its scientific approach to understanding how people’s feelings, thoughts and behaviour are influenced by the presence of others.
Close

Statistics & Experimental Methods
Teaches multivariate statistical methods for research on complex human phenomena. Topics include linear and logistic regression, factor analysis, analysis of variance and covariance, and non-parametric tests. Students select and apply models, assess statistical problems and report their analyses.
Close

Advanced Research Seminar
Advanced Research Seminar introduces systematic reviews and meta-analysis to synthesise results across studies. Students use R to conduct analyses, work with data structures and packages, estimate treatment effects and examine their consistency across studies. Presentations and active research tasks develop evidence-synthesis skills.
Close

Lifespan Developmental Psychology
Explores human development across the lifespan. Examines physical, cognitive, emotional and social changes from prenatal life to old age and develops critical thinking about factors influencing individual uniqueness.
Close
